item_name: Recovery after loss in modern trackers - MotionTrack refind module (Qin et al., CVPR 2023), OC-SORT observation-centric re-update/recovery (Cao et al., CVPR 2023), Hybrid-SORT weak cues (Yang et al., AAAI 2024)
depth_level: Short check with ablation tables (main text of all three papers, MotionTrack supplementary, OC-SORT and Hybrid-SORT code files for the recovery logic). Verdict: all three mechanisms are tracker-side and become part of the equal no-fly control. They do not modernize FlyVis. Only two ideas can be moved into fly nodes: observation-centric eye placement or state re-update after loss, and a high-precision, history-conditioned refind decision in the readout. Neither is supported yet by project data that shows where the 1001 wrong assignments sit relative to loss gaps.

Dependence: Hybrid-SORT is built on OC-SORT, uses the same YOLOX detections and keeps OCR as its third stage, so its gains are not an independent replication of OC-SORT. All three use the public ByteTrack YOLOX weights on MOT17/MOT20, so their detector inputs are shared. full_text_checked: Read in full from arXiv PDFs, with text extracted locally: MotionTrack main paper (sections 3-4, Tables 1-5, Fig. 5) and its supplementary (architecture/training details, Table 1 on error compensation, section H on correlation accuracy, Algorithm 1); OC-SORT main paper sections 4-5 (ORU, OCM, OCR, Tables 5-7) and appendix H (intuition behind ORU); Hybrid-SORT main paper (method Eq. 1-10, Tables 4-8). Code opened: OC_SORT trackers/ocsort_tracker/kalmanfilter.py (freeze()/unfreeze(), the ORU virtual trajectory with constant speed between the last two real observations) and trackers/ocsort_tracker/ocsort.py (OCR second pass: IoU between last_observation of unmatched tracks and unmatched detections, gated by iou_threshold); HybridSORT trackers/hybrid_sort_tracker/hybrid_sort.py (TCM linear confidence prediction, around lines 257-260, and the TCM_byte_step confidence-difference penalty). Not read: OC-SORT appendices A-G in detail and Tables 8-13; Hybrid-SORT benchmark Tables 1-3 in detail; any MotionTrack code (none found). Project context read: ObsidianFlyVis notes for buffer_extend_v1, association_log_v1 and tracker_zoo, plus the class_gate_v1 card in experiments/project_history.json.
inputs_state_output: MotionTrack Refind. Inputs are box coordinates only, with no image: the last 30 alive locations (t,x,y,w,h) of each lost tracklet (S x 30 x 5) and each unmatched detection, concatenated with its difference from the last alive location (10-d). State: the trajectory buffer, plus Interaction-Module predictions recorded while the track is lost. Output: an S x U correlation matrix (sigmoid) over lost tracks x leftover detections. OC-SORT. Inputs are detector boxes only. State: a Kalman filter with a frozen copy of its parameters taken at the moment of loss, and the history of real observations. ORU replays a virtual constant-speed trajectory between the last real observation z_t1 and the re-associating observation z_t2 to re-update the KF. OCR keeps the last observation box. Output: a corrected KF state, or a second-pass match. Hybrid-SORT. Inputs are detector boxes plus detection confidence. State: a KF extended with confidence c and its rate, a short memory of past confidences, and four-corner velocity directions. Output: extra cost terms (|c_trk - c_det|, height IoU multiplied into IoU, corner-direction cost) added to the assignment matrix. Comparison with ours: none of the three uses image content. Their state is trajectory geometry and confidence over 2-30 frames. Ours is a bounded grey crop through FlyVis with a recurrent state over exemplar and search frames, 68 regional features per real detection, an observed-target descriptor, 8 geometry inputs and 6 assignment-context features. Their entire signal is therefore a subset of what our no-fly geometry/context branch could contain, with two exceptions. First, our context features may lack confidence dynamics and height IoU [uncertain]. Second, we have no explicit lost-track history buffer: our temporal audit found that only 14252 of 37296 queries have a prior query with supported regions.
action_and_refusal: MotionTrack: refind acts only on lost tracks and on detections still unmatched after the primary IoU association. It never overrides a primary match. Abstention is built in: pairs with correlation below 0.9 are rejected, the rest are matched greedily, and leftover detections start new tracks. After a refind, error compensation corrects the predicted boxes during the gap (offline-style trajectory fill). OC-SORT: OCR is a second IoU pass between the last observations of unmatched tracks and unmatched detections, gated by the same IoU threshold of 0.3 (the code notes that a lower threshold, 0.2, helps on MOT17/20). ORU changes no assignment: it only re-updates the KF state after a re-association, so later predictions do not drift away again. Hybrid-SORT: weak cues only re-weight the cost matrix. Refusal stays the standard Hungarian gate with an IoU threshold of 0.15 on DanceTrack and 0.25 elsewhere. Comparison with ours: our action writes a full XYWH box into the track state before native ByteTrack matching, and it can override what ByteTrack would have matched. It is closer to a forced re-association than to their leftover-only recovery. Abstention is the fixed logit 0. All three sources apply recovery only to residuals after the primary match and use a strict gate, either a high threshold or an IoU gate. That is a design constraint we have not imposed: our policy can select 1000-3500 of 4183 rows.
labels_and_loss: MotionTrack Refind: labels are synthetic pairs from ground-truth trajectories. Trajectories in a video are coupled randomly in pairs. A tracklet and a detection are sampled, and the pair is labelled positive if both come from the same trajectory. Tracklets are longer than 20 frames, and the gap between tracklet and detection in a positive is 10-120 frames. Loss is binary cross-entropy (Eq. 9). Training uses half of the MOT17/MOT20 train set, Adam, 10 epochs, batch 64. Class balance is set by the pairing, so it is roughly balanced by construction [uncertain]. The reported 97% (MOT17) and 99% (MOT20) correlation accuracy is measured on this balanced pair protocol, not on deployment-time candidate sets. The labels are identity similarity, not the consequence of the assignment. The Interaction Module uses an IoU loss on the next-frame box. OC-SORT and Hybrid-SORT are training-free: no labels or loss, only hand-set hyperparameters (lambda 0.2, delta t 3, confidence weights 1.5/1.0 on DanceTrack and 1.0/1.0 elsewhere). None of the three models neutral events, or the asymmetric cost of a harmful re-association, in a loss. Harm control comes entirely from gating: a threshold of 0.9, an IoU gate, or residual-only application.
data_camera_resolution_rate: MotionTrack: MOT17 (7 train sequences, half-split validation; test via server) and MOT20 (4 train sequences). Cameras are static and moving; global motion compensation is applied. Detector: public ByteTrack YOLOX. The lost-track buffer is 60 frames on MOT17 and 120 on MOT20. TAO is mentioned only in the supplementary (mAP50 19.6). OC-SORT: MOT17, MOT20, KITTI (10 fps), DanceTrack (val 25 videos; nonlinear motion, similar appearance, frequent crossings, easy detection) and CroHD. Ablations are on MOT17-val (half split) and DanceTrack-val. Detection threshold 0.6 (0.4 on MOT20). Hybrid-SORT: DanceTrack, MOT17, MOT20. Ablations are on DanceTrack-val, plus MOT17-val for the generality tables. Input resolution is the YOLOX ByteTrack setting (about 1440x800 on MOT17) [uncertain]. Frame rates are 14-30 fps on MOT17 and 20 fps on DanceTrack [uncertain]. All are pedestrian or person datasets; KITTI cars appear only in OC-SORT. Each reports one run, with no seeds and no intervals. Ours: BDD100K MOT with a moving camera, at night, with glare, occlusion and mixed classes, a detector run at 960 and paired bootstrap over videos. This is a different regime: there are no DanceTrack-like uniform-appearance dancers, and camera ego-motion dominates linear-motion assumptions.

distinguishing_ablations: MotionTrack: Table 3 isolates the Refind Module, which replaces IoU refind on the KF prediction: +0.3 HOTA, one run. Table 4 is the most relevant to us. When the lost-track window grows from 30 to 120 frames, naive refind (IoU -0.6 HOTA, ReID -5.8) degrades through wrong late associations, while the learned high-threshold refind gains +0.5. The mandatory components for the claimed effect are therefore the selective decision (correlation of at least 0.9) and history-conditioned features, not the recovery attempt itself. Error compensation is nearly irrelevant (+0.1). Authors' limitation: motion-only, pedestrian interactions only. OC-SORT: cumulative ablation only, never one-at-a-time, one run. ORU is the main gain on MOT17 (+1.4 HOTA). OCM matters on DanceTrack (+3.6) and hardly on MOT17 (+0.1). OCR's marginal effect is +0.1 HOTA on MOT17 and 0.0 on DanceTrack (AssA +0.3, IDF1 +1.0). Local virtual trajectories beat fitted global ones by 2-3 HOTA (Table 6), so longer history fitted online hurt. Authors note that ORU does not change the power of the KF: it only fixes a convention of small velocity covariance. Hybrid-SORT: cumulative ablation on DanceTrack only. TCM +4.0 HOTA comes mostly from the KF confidence in the first stage (+2.9; Table 5); linear prediction alone is harmful (-1.1). Width cues hurt (-5.1), so the specific weak cue matters. On MOT17 the TCM/HMIoU gains are at most +1.0 and sometimes negative (Table 8: ByteTrack -0.2, MOTDT -0.1). Common across all three: big gains appear on DanceTrack (static camera, uniform appearance, nonlinear motion); gains on MOT17 are about 1 HOTA or less; there are no confidence intervals and no seeds.
explanations_addressed: Lost discriminative/spatial information in the readout: not addressed directly, because all three are appearance-free. As a caution, MotionTrack reaches 97% balanced pair accuracy from 30-frame box history alone, so history geometry can carry much of the identity signal; a FlyVis readout must beat such a geometry-only refind control. Target-versus-neighbour identification: Hybrid-SORT gives direct evidence on DanceTrack that confidence state (occluder versus occluded) and height IoU separate overlapping neighbours (+4.0 and +1.6 HOTA), with weak or no effect on MOT17. MotionTrack's Interaction Module models neighbour influence on motion, not identity (+0.3). Training objective mismatched to the final assignment: design analogy only. MotionTrack trains refind on identity pairs with BCE (similarity, not consequence) and still gains, but only with a 0.9 threshold and only on residuals. OC-SORT and Hybrid-SORT are untrained. None trains on assignment consequences, so they do not test our good-minus-harm objective. Rare useful events with high harm cost: direct evidence in MotionTrack Table 4. Opening more recovery opportunities without a selective decision is harmful (-0.6 and -5.8 HOTA), consistent with our buffer_extend_v1 (-0.33 HOTA after MASA). All three handle harm by strict gating and residual-only application, not by learning a calibrated advantage. Insufficient history: mixed. MotionTrack uses 30 frames of history; OC-SORT shows that richer online trajectory fits (GPR, linear regression) are worse than a 2-point constant-speed fill. More history helps a learned discriminator but not an online extrapolator. Our temporal coverage (14252 of 37296 queries with prior supported regions; oracle +2.07 pp in that subset) limits any history-based mechanism. Limits of the action: as a caution, all three recovery actions apply only to leftover tracks and detections after the primary match, plus a state fix (ORU, error compensation). None overrides a primary assignment by writing a box before matching as ours does. Our action is stronger and therefore riskier, which may explain why most selected actions are neutral or harmful.
evidence_strength: All three are peer-reviewed: CVPR 2023 (MotionTrack, OC-SORT) and AAAI 2024 (Hybrid-SORT). OC-SORT and Hybrid-SORT have code, verified in this session for the ORU, OCR and TCM logic, and are widely re-implemented (for example BoxMOT, which the project already uses). Their gains on DanceTrack have been reproduced by many later works [uncertain]. MotionTrack has no code found and an internal table inconsistency (Table 3 versus Table 4); its refind gain is +0.3 HOTA from one run. None reports seeds, intervals or per-video variance. Overall: moderate for OC-SORT and Hybrid-SORT as tracker improvements on DanceTrack-like data; weak for transfer to BDD100K, because the gains on linear-motion MOT17 are about 1 HOTA and the project already measured that its long-loss failures are mostly missing detections rather than drift; weak-moderate for the MotionTrack refind effect.
difference_from_tried: Versus our tried variants (fixed and learned 3-peak association, ridge target model, per-action MSE good-minus-harm head with a softmax-threshold policy, category replacement, context features). (a) Residual-only application: OCR and Refind only consider tracks and detections left unmatched by the primary association. Our full-box action can override the primary match for any query. This difference is real and untried as a restriction of our action space. (b) High fixed acceptance threshold on a separately trained binary same-identity score (0.9 in MotionTrack), instead of softmax against a fixed logit 0 with a threshold tuned on 20 videos. Our softmax never exceeded about 0.6, so a 0.9 gate on our score would abstain completely. The difference is the calibrated binary pair classifier, partly tried through the ridge target model. (c) Observation-centric state repair after loss (ORU): we never re-update the FlyVis recurrent state or the eye placement after a re-acquisition. During loss the state keeps updating on search frames centred on the drifting tracker prediction. This is untried and is the only mechanism here that maps onto a fly state node. (d) Weak cues (confidence dynamics, height IoU, corner direction) as context: our 6 context and 8 geometry features may already overlap partly, but confidence-trend and height IoU have not been explicitly confirmed [uncertain]. (e) Already tried at tracker level without the fly: buffer extension (buffer_extend_v1, negative) and a class gate (class_gate_v1, null); OC-SORT ORU/OCR was named as a candidate replacement on 11.10 but never run.
candidate_node_change: Classification under the project boundary. Tracker-side and not FlyVis modernization: OCR, ORU on the Kalman filter, OCM/ROCM, TCM, HMIoU, the Interaction Module and a trajectory-only refind classifier. All of these belong to the equal no-fly control. Transferable to fly nodes: (1) input preparation and state: an observation-centric eye with state re-update; (2) readout or loss: a residual-only, history-conditioned binary refind decision with a strict gate. Note that (2) is close to an external head over the fly signal; it counts as modernization only if it replaces the existing readout node rather than adding a filter on top. Primary proposal, change (1). For queries whose track has a gap of at least 1 frame since its last real observation, place the FlyVis eye on a crop covering both the KF prediction and the last observation (the OCR analogue), or on the constant-speed virtual position. After a re-acquisition, re-run the FlyVis recurrent state over virtual crops along the interpolated trajectory (the ORU analogue), so the state and the ridge exemplars are not contaminated by search frames centred on a drifted prediction. The FlyVis problem it addresses is stale or contaminated recurrent state and eye placement during loss; the mapping to a registry P-number is still to be confirmed [uncertain]. Rationale from project numbers: 334 of the 895 unfixable wrong assignments had the correct detection outside the eye, and the whole-frame full-box oracle (+7.25) exceeds the in-eye one (+5.24) by 2.01 pp. Equal controls: (i) old D, the current readout; (ii) stock C, unmodified FlyVis; (iii) eye input R1, the same new crop placement with raw crop features and no FlyVis; (iv) no-fly geometry plus tracker recovery: XYWHByteTrack with OC-SORT ORU+OCR and Hybrid-SORT TCM+HMIoU cues. This means the same full-box action, fixed logit 0 abstention and 20-video threshold selection, but driven only by geometry, confidence and last-observation features, plus a MotionTrack-style trajectory-only BCE refind classifier with a 0.9 gate on residuals. Control (iv) is the explicit equal no-fly control. By rule 6.16 a FlyVis result requires the fly variant to beat (iv), not just the stand. Cheap distinguishing check on saved data (CPU, no new FlyVis maps): stratify the 1001 wrong baseline assignments, and the 553 in-eye and 334 out-of-eye subsets, by frames since the last matched observation. For the 334, compute the fraction whose correct detection falls inside an eye centred on the last observation or on the ORU-corrected prediction. Recompute the full-box oracle reserve for that eye placement. Also run control (iv) on saved detections: OCR/ORU are training-free in BoxMOT/OC_SORT, so this is pure CPU. Proceed to GPU (new FlyVis maps for the new eye placement or the state replay) only if all three hold (these are proposed thresholds, to be registered before the run): the re-placed eye brings at least about 30% of the 334 inside; the recomputed oracle reserve exceeds +5.24 by at least 1 pp; and control (iv) leaves at least 2 pp of oracle reserve unexplained. If most wrong assignments occur with no prior gap, the loss-recovery mechanisms are irrelevant to our failure and this item should be ranked low.
strongest_objection: All three mechanisms are appearance-free tracker heuristics. Their sizeable gains appear on DanceTrack (static camera, uniform appearance, nonlinear motion, easy detection), while on linear-motion MOT17 they give about 1 HOTA or less (MotionTrack refind +0.3; OC-SORT OCR +0.1; HMIoU on ByteTrack -0.2). The project's own measurements point away from loss recovery as the main failure: long buffers hurt (-0.33 HOTA), a class gate did nothing, and 72% of wrong long-gap returns had no correct confident detection at all. Whatever these mechanisms deliver is credited to the tracker (the no-fly control), not to FlyVis. Adopting them raises the bar the fly must clear without adding any fly-specific signal. The only fly-node transfer, observation-centric eye placement and state replay, is our extrapolation, not something the sources test. Also unknown: whether the 1001 wrong assignments are mostly after loss gaps at all.
cost_and_hardware: CPU on saved data, roughly hours: gap stratification of the 1001/553/334 cases, eye-placement coverage and oracle recomputation from saved query geometry, and the training-free OC-SORT ORU+OCR / Hybrid-SORT TCM+HMIoU no-fly control on cached detections. A MotionTrack-style trajectory-only refind classifier is tiny (4 conv layers, 256-d) and trains on CPU in minutes to hours [uncertain]. GPU (one 12 GB card, single CUDA process): needed only for new FlyVis maps with the re-placed eye or the state replay along virtual crops. Expected cost is comparable to one existing map extraction pass over train26 plus the evaluation videos; exact hours were not measured here [uncertain]. Must respect the 07:40 MSK weekday stop.
